section.heading: Department of Motor Vehicles' authority to restrict, suspend, or revoke driving privileges for good cause; reciprocity; penalties.

para.text: In addition to any other authority provided under District law, the DMV may for good cause:
Suspend or revoke a person's license; or
Suspend or revoke a nonresident person's privilege to operate a motor vehicle in the District of Columbia.
Prior to taking any action pursuant subsection (a) of this section, the DMV shall:
That the DMV is seeking to take one of the actions described in subsection (a) of this section;
Of the DMV's rationale for taking the proposed action;
That the person has 10 business days from the time of notice to request a hearing with the DMV to contest the proposed action; and
That failure to request a hearing within 10 business days shall result in the proposed action being taken.

In cases where the DMV is seeking to revoke a nonresident person's privilege to operate a motor vehicle in the District of Columbia as described in subsection (a)(2) of this section, notify the state or territorial agency that has issued the nonresident person's license.

For the purposes of this subsection, the person shall be considered to have been provided notice upon receipt of a letter containing the information described in paragraph (1)(A) of this subsection that is either:
Hand delivered to the person; or
Delivered by certified mail to the address listed on the person's license.
The DMV shall suspend the license and registrations of a District resident if:
The DMV receives a certification from any state that it has suspended or revoked the operating privilege of that District resident; and

The suspension or revocation was based on a conviction for, or a forfeiture of any bond or collateral related to, an offense that, if committed in the District, would require the DMV to suspend a nonresident's operating privilege.
Any restriction, suspension, or revocation of a license imposed under this section shall be for a period determined by the DMV but shall not exceed 5 years.
This section shall be subject to the requirements of Chapter 5 of Title 2.

An individual found guilty of operating a motor vehicle in the District during the period for which the individual's license is revoked or suspended, or for which his right to operate is suspended or revoked, shall, for each such offense, be fined no more than the amount set forth in § 22-3571.01, or incarcerated for no more than one year, or both.

annotations.annotation: This section originated at a time when local government powers were delegated to a Board of Commissioners of the District of Columbia (see Acts Relating to the Establishment of the District of Columbia and its Various Forms of Governmental Organization in Volume 1). Section 401 of Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1967 (see Reorganization Plans in Volume 1) transferred all of the functions of the Board of Commissioners under this section to a single Commissioner. The District of Columbia Self-Government and Governmental Reorganization Act, 87 Stat. 818, § 711 ( D.C. Code, § 1-207.11), abolished the District of Columbia Council and the Office of Commissioner of the District of Columbia. These branches of government were replaced by the Council of the District of Columbia and the Office of Mayor of the District of Columbia, respectively. Accordingly, and also pursuant to § 714(a) of such Act ( D.C. Code, § 1-207.14(a)), appropriate changes in terminology were made in this section.
